title: Min Stack
prompt:
Design a stack that supports `push`, `pop`, `top`, and retrieving the minimum element — **all in O(1)**.

- `MinStack()` — construct
- `void push(int val)`
- `void pop()`
- `int top()`
- `int getMin()` — the minimum across the whole stack

**Constraints**: `pop`, `top`, and `getMin` are only called on a non-empty stack; values fit in an `int`.
hints: A single `min` variable breaks on pop: if you pop the current minimum, what was the minimum before it was pushed? What if each entry remembered that?
Store with every value the minimum of the stack at the moment it was pushed (or keep a second stack of those minimums). Popping then restores the old minimum automatically.
Push `new int[]{val, stack.isEmpty() ? val : Math.min(val, stack.peek()[1])}` onto a `Deque<int[]>`; getMin is `stack.peek()[1]`.

solution.explanation: Insight: a stack's contents below any entry never change while that entry is on top, so the minimum at push time stays correct for as long as the entry exists. Each entry stores the minimum of itself and everything below it, so after a pop the new top already holds the previous minimum. Duplicate minimums work because each copy stores its own snapshot. All operations O(1) time; space O(n).
